_why: The premade build already carries most of the Destruction redesign --
Sacrifice the Weak, Molten Rain, Burning Soul, Aftermath and the generating
Shadowburn -- but it stops short of the two talents that let the shard
economy be spent, and it leaves two points unspent (69 of 71).
Infernal Bargain 1/1     (T5.2) the dump. A five-second channel costing
1/2/4/8/16 shards per second, granting +3% damage
and +1% spell crit per shard spent, and total
immunity to damage while it runs. The burst
button and the panic button are the same button.
Wailing Souls 3/3        (T5.0) Searing Pain converts a shard into 15%
damage reduction, to three stacks. The cheap
half of the same economy, for when the bar is
not deep enough to bargain with.
Improved Searing Pain 3/3 (T3.3) Searing Pain is the Wailing Souls
generator now rather than a threat tool, so its
crit talent feeds the mitigation directly.
Funded entirely by the 5-point Demonology dip, which this build cannot use
at all: Sacrifice the Weak sacrifices the pet permanently in exchange for
Nathrezim Foresight, and both Imperious Flames (an Imp buff) and Fel Synergy
(pet healing) need a pet to exist. The premade build takes Sacrifice the
Weak and the pet talents at the same time, which is a contradiction it can
afford in a raid and cannot afford alone.
Note what is NOT bought. Nathrezim Foresight already pays 1% damage
reduction and 1% spell crit damage per shard carried, resynced every second,
so shards are never idle and there is no reason to buy a second way to hold
them. Molten Rain and Ruin's Immolate spread are both AoE and invisible to
the single-target simulator; they are left exactly as the premade build has
them rather than tuned blind.
5 Affliction / 66 Destruction.
